ichnoscopy: The search for the traces of anything.
ichthyosaurus: An extinct genus of marine reptiles; -- so named from their short, biconcave vertebræ, resembling those of fishes. Several species, varying in length from ten to thirty feet, are known from the Liassic, Oölitic, and Cretaceous formations.
ichthyophagist: One who eats, or subsists on, fish.
icypearled: Spangled with ice. Mounting up in icy-pearled car. Milton. I'D I'd . A contraction from I would or I had.
icosandrian: Pertaining to the class Icosandria; having twenty or more stamens inserted in the calyx.
iconomania: A mania or infatuation for icons, whether as objects of devotion, bric-a-brac, or curios.
ichthyotomy: The anatomy or dissection of fishes.
iconize: To form an image or likeness of. Cudworth.
ictus: 1. (Pros.) The stress of voice laid upon accented syllable of a word. Cf. Arsis. 2. (Med.) A stroke or blow, as in a sunstroke, the sting of an insect, pulsation of an artery, etc.
ichthyomorphic: Fish-shaped; as, the ichthyomorphic idols of ancient Assyria.
ichthyopsida: A grand division of the Vertebrata, including the Amphibia and Fishes.
icily: In an icy manner; coldly. Faultily faultless, icily regular, splendidly null, Dead perfection, no more. Tennyson.
ic: 1. A suffix signifying, in general, relating to, or characteristic of; as, historic, hygienic, telegraphic, etc. 2. (Chem.) A suffix, denoting that the element indicated enters into certain compounds with its highest valence, or with a valence relatively higher than in compounds where the name of the element ends in -ous; as, ferric, sulphuric.
iconoclasm: The doctrine or practice of the iconoclasts; image breaking.
icefall: A frozen waterfall, or mass of ice resembling a frozen waterfall. Coleridge.
ichthyosauria: An extinct order of marine reptiles, including Ichthyosaurus and allied forms; -- called also Ichthyopterygia. They have not been found later than the Cretaceous period.
icteroid: Of a tint resembling that produced by jaundice; yellow; as, an icteroid tint or complexion.
icicle: A pendent, and usually conical, mass of ice, formed by freezing of dripping water; as, the icicles on the eaves of a house.
iconograph: An engraving or other picture or illustration for a book.
icequake: The crash or concussion attending the breaking up of masses of ice, -- often due to contraction from extreme cold.
iconodule: One who serves images; -- opposed to an iconoclast. Schaff- Herzog Encyc.
ichthyodorulite: One of the spiny plates foundon the back and tail of certain skates.
ichthyolite: A fossil fish, or fragment of a fish.
ichthin: A nitrogenous substance resembling vitellin, present in the egg yolk of cartilaginous fishes.
ichthulin: A substance from the yolk of salmon's egg.
icelandic: Of or pertaining to Iceland; relating to, or resembling, the Icelanders. | The language of the Icelanders. It is one of the Scandinavian group, and is more nearly allied to the Old Norse than any other language now spoken.
iconoclast: 1. A breaker or destroyer of images or idols; a determined enemy of idol worship. 2. One who exposes or destroys impositions or shams; one who attacks cherished beliefs; a radical.
icebird: An Arctic sea bird, as the Arctic fulmar.
icing: A coating or covering resembling ice, as of sugar and milk or white of egg; frosting.
ichnographical: Of or pertaining to ichonography; describing a ground plot.
ichthyocolla: Fish glue; isinglass; a glue prepared from the sounds of certain fishes.
iceman: 1. A man who is skilled in traveling upon ice, as among glaciers. 2. One who deals in ice; one who retails or delivers ice.
ichthyomancy: Divination by the heads or the entrails of fishes.
iconographic: 1. Of or pertaining to iconography. 2. Representing by means of pictures or diagrams; as, an icongraphic encyclopædia.
icelander: A native, or one of the Scandinavian people, of Iceland.
ichnographic: Of or pertaining to ichonography; describing a ground plot.
ichorhaemia: Infection of the blood with ichorous or putrid substances.
ichor: 1. (Class. Myth.) An ethereal fluid that supplied the place of blood in the veins of the gods. 2. A thin, acrid, watery discharge from an ulcer, wound, etc.
ichorous: Of or like ichor; thin; watery; serous; sanious.
ichthyornis: An extinct genus of toothed birds found in the American Cretaceous formation. It is remarkable for having biconcave vertebræ, and sharp, conical teeth set in sockets. Its wings were well developed. It is the type of the order Odontotormæ.
ichnography: A horizontal section of a building or other object, showing its true dimensions according to a geometric scale; a ground plan; a map; also, the art of making such plans.
ichthidin: A substance from the egg yolk of osseous fishes.
ichthyomorphous: Fish-shaped; as, the ichthyomorphic idols of ancient Assyria.
icarian: Soaring too high for safety, like Icarus; adventurous in flight.
icterical: 1. Pertaining to, or affected with, jaundice. 2. Good against the jaundice. Johnson.
iconology: The discussion or description of portraiture or of representative images. Cf. Iconography.
iceberg: A large mass of ice, generally floating in the ocean. Note: Icebergs are large detached portions of glaciers, which in cold regions often project into the sea.
ichthyophthira: A division of copepod crustaceans, including numerous species parasitic on fishes.
icosahedral: Having twenty equal sides or faces.
iced: 1. Covered with ice; chilled with ice; as, iced water. 2. Covered with something resembling ice, as sugar icing; frosted; as, iced cake. Iced cream. Same as Ice cream, under Ice.
iconism: The formation of a figure, representation, or semblance; a delineation or description. Some kind of apish imitations, counterfeit iconisms. Cudworth.
icy: 1. Pertaining to, resembling, or abounding in, ice; cold; frosty. "Icy chains." Shak. "Icy region." Boyle. "Icy seas." Pope. 2. Characterized by coldness, as of manner, influence, etc.; chilling; frigid; cold. Icy was the deportment with which Philip received these demonstrations of affection. Motley.
ichthyosis: A disease in which the skin is thick, rough, and scaly; -- called also fishskin. -- Ich`thy*ot"ic, a.
iciness: The state or quality of being icy or very cold; frigidity.
iceplant: A plant (Mesembryanthemum crystallinum), sprinkled with pellucid, watery vesicles, which glisten like ice. It is native along the Mediterranean, in the Canaries, and in South Africa. Its juice is said to be demulcent and diuretic; its ashes are used in Spain in making glass. Ice-skater = one who skates on ice wearing an ice skate; esp.
icositetrahedron: A twenty-four-sided solid; a tetragonal trisoctahedron or trapezohedron.
icteric: 1. Pertaining to, or affected with, jaundice. 2. Good against the jaundice. Johnson.
icteritious: Yellow; of the color of the skin when it is affected by the jaundice.
ichthyopterygium: The typical limb, or lateral fin, of fishes.
ichthyophagy: The practice of eating, or living upon, fish.
iconolatry: The worship of images as symbols; -- distinguished from idolatry, the worship of images themselves.
ichthyology: The natural history of fishes; that branch of zoölogy which relates to fishes, including their structure, classification, and habits.
ichnology: The branch of science which treats of fossil footprints.
ich: I. (old) Chaucer. Note: In the Southern dialect of Early English this is the regular form. Cf. Ik.
icosandria: A Linnæan class of plants, having twenty or more stamens inserted in the calyx.
icosandrous: Pertaining to the class Icosandria; having twenty or more stamens inserted in the calyx.
ichthyoid: Somewhat like a fish; having some of the characteristics of fishes; -- said of some amphibians.
iconography: 1. The art or representation by pictures or images; the description or study of portraiture or representation, as of persons; as, the iconography of the ancients. 2. The study of representative art in general. Christian iconography, the study of the representations in art of the Deity, the persons of the Trinity, angels, saints, virtues, vices, etc.
iconical: Pertaining to, or consisting of, images, pictures, or representations of any kind.
ichthyol: An oily substance prepared by the dry distillation of a bituminous mineral containing fossil fishes. It is used in medicine as a remedy in some forms of skin diseases.
ichthyolatry: Worship of fishes, or of fish-shaped idols. Layard.
ichnite: A fossil footprint; as, the ichnites in the Triassic sandstone. Page.
ichthyologist: One versed in, or who studies, ichthyology.
ichneumon: 1. (Zoöl.) Any carnivorous mammal of the genus Herpestes, and family Viverridæ. Numerous species are found in Asia and Africa. The Egyptian species(H. ichneumon), which ranges to Spain and Palestine, is noted for destroying the eggs and young of the crocodile as well as various snakes and lizards, and hence was considered sacred by the ancient Egyptians.
icelandspar: A transparent variety of calcite, the best of which is obtained in Iceland. It is used for the prisms of the polariscope, because of its strong double refraction. Cf. Calcite.
iconophilist: A student, or lover of the study, of iconography.
icebuilt: 1. Composed of ice. 2. Loaded with ice. "Ice-built mountains." Gray.
icteritous: Yellow; of the color of the skin when it is affected by the jaundice.
ice: 1. Water or other fluid frozen or reduced to the solid state by cold; frozen water. It is a white or transparent colorless substance, crystalline, brittle, and viscoidal. | 1. To cover with ice; to convert into ice, or into something resembling ice. 2. To cover with icing, or frosting made of sugar and milk or white of egg; to frost, as cakes, tarts, etc. 3.
iconomical: Opposed to pictures or images as objects of worship. Sir T. Browne.
ichthyosaurian: Of or pertaining to the Ichthyosauria. -- n. One of the Ichthyosauria.
ichthyoidal: Somewhat like a fish; having some of the characteristics of fishes; -- said of some amphibians.
ictic: Pertaining to, or caused by, a blow; sudden; abrupt. H. Bushnell.
iconomachy: Hostility to images as objects of worship.
icebound: Totally surrounded with ice, so as to be incapable of advancing; as, an icebound vessel; also, surrounded by or fringed with ice so as to hinder easy access; as, an icebound coast.
iconodulist: One who serves images; -- opposed to an iconoclast. Schaff- Herzog Encyc.
ichthyocol: Fish glue; isinglass; a glue prepared from the sounds of certain fishes.
icosahedron: A solid bounded by twenty sides or faces. Regular icosahedron, one of the five regular polyhedrons, bounded by twenty equilateral triangules. Five triangules meet to form each solid angle of the polyhedron.
icon: An image or representation; a portrait or pretended portrait. Netherlands whose names and icons are published. Hakewill.
ics: . A suffix used in forming the names of certain sciences, systems, etc., as acoustics, mathematics, dynamics, statistics, politics, athletics. Note: The names sciences ending in ics, as mathematics, mechanics, metaphysics, optics, etc., are, with respect to their form, nouns in the plural number.
ichneumonidan: Of or pertaining to the Ichneumonidæ, or ichneumon flies. -- n. One of the Ichneumonidæ.
iconoclastic: Of or pertaining to the iconoclasts, or to image breaking. Milman.
ichthus: In early Christian and eccesiastical art, an emblematic fish, or the Greek word for fish, which combined the initials of the Greek words
icelandmoss: A kind of lichen (Cetraria Icelandica) found from the Arctic regions to the North Temperate zone. It furnishes a nutritious jelly and other forms of food, and is used in pulmonary complaints as a demulcent.
